title: Chile’s cultural participation is high in aggregate but sharply constrained by age, socioeconomic status, disability, and time
source_unit: Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas de Chile and Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage, National Survey of Cultural Participation and Reading Behavior 2024
geography: Chile; urban residents aged 15 and over, with age, socioeconomic, education, disability, sex, and household-composition dimensions

observations.period: 2024; cultural participation during the previous 12 months

denominator.unit: approximately 18,500 selected urban households planned for the ENPCCL fieldwork; published results are weighted population estimates

any_cultural_participation.unit: percent of people aged 15+ participating in at least one cultural activity in the previous 12 months

young_event_attendance.unit: percent of younger people attending cultural shows/events, as reported in the release's age comparison

older_event_attendance.unit: percent of older people attending cultural shows/events, as reported in the release's age comparison

disability_participation.unit: percent among people with a disability status

no_disability_participation.unit: percent among people without a disability status

disability_participation_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between people without and with disability status

mechanism.value: Aggregate cultural participation conceals a large opportunity gradient: age, socioeconomic resources, education, and disability shape who can convert cultural desire into attendance

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the Chilean ENPCCL 2024 release and results synthesis; subgroup values and the disability gap are published or calculated from published percentages.
observations.uncertainty: The survey covers urban areas and uses annual-recall self-reports; the age comparison in the public release refers to cultural shows/events and should not be treated as identical to the aggregate any-activity indicator without consulting the detailed tables.
observations.subgroup: Urban residents aged 15 and over in Chile, by age, socioeconomic status, education, sex, and disability status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences may combine income, transport, health, caregiving, education, cultural supply, household composition, and measurement of what counts as participation; they do not establish a single causal barrier.

observations.period: 2024; unmet cultural demand and reading behavior

denominator.unit: approximately 18,500 selected urban households planned for the ENPCCL fieldwork; published results are weighted population estimates

wanted_but_could_not_attend.unit: percent of people who wanted to attend a cultural activity or infrastructure but did not during 2024

time_or_fatigue_reason.unit: percent among those with unmet cultural demand identifying lack of time or fatigue

economic_reason.unit: percent among those with unmet cultural demand identifying economic reasons

work_or_study_reason.unit: percent among those with unmet cultural demand identifying work or study

reading_15_minutes.unit: percent reading books, magazines, newspapers, or comics for at least 15 continuous minutes in the previous 12 months

books_read_for_pleasure.unit: average books read for pleasure or leisure in the previous 12 months

mechanism.value: The hidden price of culture is often time and exhaustion before money: among people who wanted to participate but could not, lack of time/fatigue was the most common reason, ahead of economic barriers

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the ENPCCL 2024 release; unmet-demand reasons are conditional shares among people reporting a desire to attend but no attendance.
observations.uncertainty: Reasons are self-reported and may overlap or reflect multiple constraints; the survey does not establish whether time scarcity arises from paid work, unpaid care, transport, scheduling, health, or household demands.
observations.subgroup: Urban residents aged 15 and over in Chile, with unmet cultural demand and reading-practice measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may report time/fatigue as a convenient explanation for low interest or supply mismatch, and reading is not a direct substitute for live cultural participation.

related_sources.claim: Official 67-page ENPCCL 2024 results synthesis containing participation, subgroup, unmet-demand, reading, and methodological details.
INE Chile survey-design page describing the target population, collection period, approximate sample, and confidentiality.

boundary: This record adds a Chilean cultural-participation, unmet-demand, time constraint, socioeconomic, disability, and reading layer. It does not establish causal barriers, national rural participation, cultural quality, household spending, or individual-level reasons beyond self-reported survey categories.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: INE Chile data page, release summary, survey-design page, and 67-page results synthesis reviewed; participation, age/SES/disability gradients, unmet-demand reasons, reading measures, urban coverage, sample, and conditional-denominator boundaries checked.
